document.title: HyperGeoJSON Viewer
lede: TypeScript types that extend GeoJSON to any number of dimensions. The rings of a polygon become the faces of a polyhedron, then the cells of a polychoron, and so on: one level of nesting for each dimension.
viewer.intro: Polytopes of any dimension, drawn as their shadows. Each small view keeps two axes and drops the rest, as in a three-view drawing. The large view gives every axis an equal share. Point at a vertex to follow it through all the views, and drag to turn the object.
install.heading: Install
install.note: Not on npm yet, so this installs straight from GitHub. The GeoJSON types it builds on come with it.
usage.heading: Usage
usage.intro: Import what you need with import type. The package holds types only, so nothing is added to your code at run time.
usage.solid: A solid is a list of faces, each a polygon turned to face outward.
usage.feature: Features carry polyhedra, polychora and higher polytopes, and the nesting tells TypeScript how deep to look.
usage.check: Get the nesting wrong and TypeScript tells you.
viewer.heading: Viewer
petrie.title: Petrie view
petrie.caption: Every axis is spread evenly over half a turn, the way an isometric drawing spreads three.
coordinate.title: Coordinate views
coordinate.caption: Views in a column share their horizontal axis, views in a row their vertical axis.
facet.label: {name} {index}
readout.hint: Point at a vertex to follow it through every view. Point at a facet above to pick it out.
footer.normals: Ochre ticks are normals. They show which way each boundary faces: away from the solid, and so into the void of the hollow cube. Every sample follows the [orientation rule].
footer.drop: Drop any HyperGeoJSON file on the page to draw it. Types and source: [kamataryo/types__hyper-geojson].
source.heading: Source
source.hint: Edit the HyperGeoJSON below and the drawing follows as you type. Tab and Shift+Tab indent and outdent; press Esc, then Tab, to leave the editor.
issues.stale: The drawing shows the last version without errors.
